# Security and quality audit - Chairside booking app

**App:** "Chairside", a salon/barbershop booking app generated by [Lovable](https://lovable.dev) from a single plain-language prompt (the prompt is in the repository README). No security requirements, access rules, or technology were specified in the prompt.

**Scope:** only a locally running copy of the app and **a separate test Supabase project** (the same database migration applied to it). No requests were made to any hosted or production environment. All test data is fictitious (`example.test`).

**What this document contains:** the findings, the evidence for each (file:line and a runnable test), the impact in plain language, the fix applied (or why it was left as a recommendation), and how to reproduce everything. Finding ids, severities, evidence and test names match the test suite in [`tests/`](tests).

---

## 1. Summary

The generated app gets the security foundations right: **row-level security (RLS) is enabled on all six tables, tenants are genuinely isolated, and double-booking is prevented by a database exclusion constraint** (all verified with tests, see "What was done well"). Lovable's own security scan reported no issues; its report also notes that *"The scanner can't catch every possible risk"* (screenshot: [`../docs/lovable-security-scan.png`](../docs/lovable-security-scan.png)).

The findings sit at a finer level: **business rules are enforced only in the browser UI, not in the database/server**, so a client that calls the API directly (bypassing the UI) can do things the UI never offers.

### Findings by severity

| Severity | Count | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | 0 | - |
| **High** | 2 | SEC-01, BH-02 |
| **Medium** | 11 | BH-01, SEC-02, SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-05, SEC-06, SEC-10, SE-01, SE-02, SE-03, SE-04 |
| **Low** | 5 | SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SE-05 |
| **Informational** | 1 | SEC-08 |

### Severity rubric

Findings are rated on one scale, by who could exploit the issue and what it affects (not by how hard it was to fix). Each finding below states its rating with a one-line rationale.

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Critical** | An anonymous, unauthenticated attacker can read or alter data across salons, or take over accounts, with little effort. |
| **High** | An anonymous or low-privilege caller, by calling the API directly, can read or change another party's personal data, or deny a core business function (e.g. the booking calendar) - with no insider action. |
| **Medium** | Needs a valid account, a specific piece of knowledge, or an insider step; or the impact is recoverable integrity/availability; or it is a defence-in-depth gap that requires a second flaw to exploit. |
| **Low** | Limited or hard-to-reach impact, or a best-practice / hygiene / maintainability gap. |
| **Informational** | No practical security impact; recorded for completeness. |

**Re-rating note (2026-10-12):** against this rubric, **BH-02** (unbounded flooding of the booking calendar - denial of a core function by an anonymous caller) was raised from Medium to **High**, and **BH-01** (out-of-policy public bookings - recoverable integrity, no data exposure) was lowered from High to **Medium**. The High/Medium/Low/Info totals are unchanged (2 / 11 / 5 / 1).

### Top 5 (one line each)

1. **SEC-01 (High)** - Without signing in, someone who knows a customer's phone number could change that customer's name and email.
2. **BH-02 (High)** - No rate limit on public bookings: a single anonymous visitor could flood the calendar and customer table and make the salon unusable.
3. **SEC-03 (Medium)** - Staff could do more than the UI showed: delete customers (which also deleted their whole history) and read every booking in the salon.
4. **BH-01 (Medium)** - Public bookings had no server-side rules: a booking at 03:00, on a closed day, or in the year 2099 was accepted (rules lived only in the UI).
5. **SEC-04 (Medium)** - No invite consent: an owner typing your email silently made you a member of that salon on your next sign-in, with read access to its customer data.

### Fix outcome

Fixes were made test-first (a failing test that proves the finding, then the smallest change, then a passing test), one commit per finding. Schema changes live in a new migration, `drizzle/migrations/0001_audit_hardening.sql`; the original migration `0000_migration.sql` is untouched so the before/after comparison is preserved.

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| SEC-01 customer overwrite | Partially fixed (name/email no longer overwritten; phone-keyed linkage is residual, `booked_name` signal added) |
| BH-01 unconstrained booking + SE-02 time zone | Fixed (salon time zone + server-side rules + slot builder) |
| SEC-02 input validation | Fixed |
| SEC-03 staff permissions | Fixed |
| SEC-04 invite consent | Fixed (explicit acceptance) |
| BH-02 quotas | Partially fixed (server-side quotas; IP/CAPTCHA + AI quota recommended) |
| SEC-05 security headers | Fixed (CSP verified against the running app) |
| SEC-07 slug + non-negative price | Fixed |
| SEC-08 helper-function grants | Fixed |
| SEC-09 AI prompt injection | Mitigated (data isolation + URL stripping; fencing is best-effort, no live exploit reproduced) |
| SEC-10 privacy | Partially fixed (booking-page notice; retention/erasure recommended) |
| Hardening: anon table grants | Fixed |
| Hardening: phone normalization | Fixed |
| SEC-06, SEC-11, SE-03, SE-05 | Left as recommendations (reasons below) |

Test suite after fixes: **42 tests, 41 pass, 1 skipped** (the skipped one is a time-zone demonstration that is meaningless when the machine is already on Europe/Istanbul). `npm run build` passes.

### Design decisions

Some behaviour is deliberate and is **not** treated as a finding:

- **Owner/staff booking management is not bound by the public booking rules.** The server-side opening-hours, open-day and 21-day checks added in BH-01 apply to the public `create_public_booking` path only. When an owner or staff member creates, moves or cancels a booking inside the signed-in app (`src/routes/_authenticated/bookings.tsx`), that path writes to `bookings` directly and is intentionally allowed to place appointments outside opening hours and on closed days - salons routinely take off-hours and day-off appointments, so the owner keeps full discretion over their own calendar. This is a product decision by the owner, not an oversight. The database exclusion constraint still prevents overlapping (double-booked) appointments on every path, and tenant isolation (RLS) still applies. A salon that later wants hard limits on staff entries too can move those writes behind an authenticated booking RPC and reuse the same checks.

## 2. Test environment

- The same migration (`drizzle/migrations/0000_migration.sql`) was applied, unchanged, to a separate test Supabase project.
- Access-control and RPC behaviour were tested both **directly against Postgres** and over **HTTP (supabase-js)**. The direct-Postgres method reproduces RLS faithfully by doing exactly what the API layer does per request: `set local role <anon|authenticated>` plus `request.jwt.claims` (and `auth.uid()` reads that claim). This is authoritative for RLS; the HTTP tests produced the same results.
- Not available in this local setup (and therefore not exercised): Google OAuth sign-in and the hosted AI gateway. The auth settings of the test project may differ from a production project; GoTrue values reported under SEC-12 are those of the test project.
- Test users were created directly in the database (email pre-confirmed, no email sent); all data is fictitious (`example.test`).
- The prompt-injection surface (SEC-09) was assessed from code plus an equivalent call to a separate model (Gemini) used purely as a test tool, since the app's hosted gateway is not reachable locally.

### Reproduce

Connection values live in a local `.env.audit` file (not committed; see `.env.example` for the variable names). Apply the schema and fixtures to your own test Supabase project, then run the suite:

```sh
npm install
psql "$AUDIT_DATABASE_URL" -f drizzle/migrations/0000_migration.sql       # before: the generated schema
psql "$AUDIT_DATABASE_URL" -f drizzle/migrations/0001_audit_hardening.sql  # after: the fixes
psql "$AUDIT_DATABASE_URL" -f audit/tests/00_fixtures.sql                  # fictitious test data
npx vitest run --config audit/vitest.config.ts                            # evidence + defense tests
```

Run with only `0000` applied and the finding tests go **red** (they prove the finding); with `0001` applied they go **green** (they prove the fix).

---

## 3. Role matrix (summary)

Full matrix with real per-persona calls: [`role-matrix.md`](role-matrix.md). Target = Salon A data.

- **anon / X / B** cannot read or write any of Salon A's tables. **Tenant isolation holds.** After the hardening, anon has no direct table privileges at all (hard `permission denied`); public reads happen only through the security-definer RPCs.
- **A (owner)** manages everything (expected).
- **A1/A2 (staff)** can **read** customers (needed to add notes) but after the fix cannot insert/update/delete them, and each staff member sees only their **own** bookings.

---

## 4. Findings

Each: **Severity** (rationale) · **Evidence** (file:line + test) · **Impact** · **Fix** · **Status**.

### Access control & abuse (SEC / BH)

#### SEC-01 - A visitor could change an existing customer's name/email · **High** (anon can alter a customer's stored personal data through the public booking RPC with no insider action; only the phone number is needed)
- **Evidence:** `drizzle/migrations/0000_migration.sql:161-163` - `create_public_booking` did `on conflict (salon_id, phone) do update set name = excluded.name, email = coalesce(...)`. Test: `audit/tests/public-booking.test.ts` and `audit/tests/http-e2e.test.ts` (`[#1]`). Reproduced: `Real Customer / real@example.test` became `HACKED NAME / attacker@evil.test` via an anonymous booking.
- **Impact:** Anyone who knows (or guesses) a customer's phone number could overwrite that customer's stored name and email; a new booking attaches to that customer's history and notes.
- **Fix / Status: Partially fixed** (`0001_audit_hardening.sql`, SEC-01). The on-conflict no longer overwrites name/email (`coalesce(nullif(customers.name,''), excluded.name)`); DB + HTTP `#1` tests are green. **Residual:** because phone is still the customer key, a booking made with a different name still links to the same phone-keyed customer (without changing it). A lightweight signal was added - `bookings.booked_name` records the name entered at booking time and the client screen shows "booked as ..." when it differs, so staff can verify. A full fix needs phone verification (OTP) at booking time (recommended).

#### BH-01 - Public bookings had no server-side rules · **Medium** (anonymous, but the damage is recoverable calendar integrity with no data exposure; re-rated from High per the rubric)
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:154-170` (only check was `_starts < now()`); opening hours / open days / 21-day window lived only in `src/lib/format.ts` and `src/routes/book.$slug.tsx`. Tests (`audit/tests/public-booking.test.ts`): booking at 03:00, in 2099, and on a closed day were all accepted.
- **Impact:** A client bypassing the UI could create appointments while the salon is closed, outside opening hours, or years in the future; the calendar stops reflecting reality.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001`, BH-01 + SE-02). A `timezone` column was added to `salons` (default `Europe/Istanbul`); `create_public_booking` now validates open day, opening hours, a 21-day advance window, and a 15-minute slot alignment (matching the UI step, anchored at `open_time`) **in the salon's time zone**. Tests green. **Scope:** these rules bind the public booking path; owner/staff bookings created or moved inside the app are intentionally not constrained to opening hours (see [Design decisions](#design-decisions)).

#### BH-02 - No rate limit / quota on public bookings · **High** (an anonymous caller can deny the core booking function by unbounded flooding; only partially mitigated; re-rated from Medium per the rubric)
- **Evidence:** `audit/tests/public-booking.test.ts` - a single anonymous caller created 60/60 bookings unthrottled. No per-user AI limit either (`src/lib/ai.functions.ts`).
- **Impact:** An attacker could fill the calendar and customer table with fake records and make the salon unusable.
- **Fix / Status: Partially fixed** (`0001`, BH-02). `create_public_booking` now enforces at most 5 upcoming bookings per phone and at most 10 bookings per salon per minute. Tests green. **Recommended (not done):** per-IP rate limiting and CAPTCHA (cannot live in the RPC because it is called directly from the browser; needs an edge layer) and a per-user/salon AI quota.

#### SEC-02 - No length/format validation on public bookings · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:156` set only a minimum length; no maximum and no email/phone format. Test: a 20,000-character name was accepted.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001`, SEC-02). `create_public_booking` now bounds name (<=120), phone (<=32, format-checked) and email (<=200, format-checked). Test green.

#### SEC-03 - Staff could do more than "see their own calendar" · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:100` (`members manage customers` granted all operations to any member), `:102` (members could read every booking); customer FKs cascade (`:50`,`:63`) so deleting a customer also deletes their bookings and notes. Tests (`audit/tests/role-matrix.test.ts`, `http-e2e.test.ts`): staff A1 edited and deleted customers.
- **Impact:** Any stylist could delete a customer and wipe that customer's entire history for the salon, and could see other staff members' clients.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001`, SEC-03). Customer writes/deletes are owner-only (`members read customers` for select + `owner manages customers` for all); bookings: each staff member reads only their own (`staff reads own bookings`), owner reads all. Tests green. Customer deletes are now owner-only (the FK cascade remains; a soft-delete to preserve history is recommended). **Residual:** staff retain read access to the full customer directory (names/phone/email/notes) - needed to keep notes; only their booking view is scoped to their own. Scoping the directory per staff member is a separate product decision (see `role-matrix.md`, `customers.select` = ✓ for staff).

#### SEC-04 - Invites auto-linked by email, without consent · **Medium** (exposes a salon's customer data, but requires an owner to enter the email, so it is not attacker-triggered; a consent/access defect)
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:110-117` (`claim_staff_invites`), called on every sign-in in `src/hooks/use-me.ts`. Test (`audit/tests/pentest.test.ts`): owner B added X's email as staff in Salon B; on X's sign-in, X became a member and could read Salon B's customers.
- **Impact:** No acceptance step. An email typed by an owner silently binds that person to the salon on sign-in, exposing that salon's customer/booking/notes data to them.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001` + `use-me.ts` + `app-shell.tsx`, SEC-04). Auto-linking removed; new RPCs `list_staff_invites()` and `accept_staff_invite(_staff)` (guarded by an email match) plus an "Accept" button on onboarding. Tests green (no auto-join; cannot accept someone else's invite; invited user can accept their own).

#### SEC-05 - No security response headers · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** no header configuration anywhere; the local response carried no CSP / X-Frame-Options / HSTS / Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy / X-Content-Type-Options.
- **Impact:** clickjacking, weaker XSS containment, no HSTS.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`src/lib/security-headers.ts` + `src/server.ts`). Every server response now carries CSP, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS. The CSP was verified against the running app (booking and sign-in pages load with no violations). Verifying live surfaced a real need: the app creates a `blob:` Web Worker (from supabase-realtime), so `worker-src 'self' blob:` was added - otherwise the CSP would have broken the app. **Known trade-off:** `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` is allowed because the framework injects inline hydration scripts; a nonce-based policy is a recommended follow-up. Test: `audit/tests/security-headers.test.ts`.

#### SEC-06 - Session token in localStorage · **Medium** (defense-in-depth)
- **Evidence:** `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` (`persistSession: true`), supabase-js default storage.
- **Impact:** combined with any XSS, both access and refresh tokens could be stolen (account takeover). Note: React's auto-escaping blocks stored XSS in names/notes, reducing the practical risk.
- **Fix / Status: Left as recommendation.** Move to an HttpOnly cookie session; strong CSP (SEC-05) and React escaping mitigate in the meantime.

#### SEC-07 - Slug not sanitized in the RPC · **Low**
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:127` (`lower(_slug)` only); the UI slugify is bypassed when the RPC is called directly. Test: `../Evil Slug!!` was stored as `../evil slug!!`.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001`, SEC-07). `create_salon` normalizes the slug and a `^[a-z0-9-]+$` CHECK constraint enforces a safe shape on every write path. Also added: non-negative price CHECK constraints on `services`/`bookings` (negative prices are now rejected). Tests green.

#### SEC-08 - Helper functions executable by anon · **Informational**
- **Evidence:** `0000_migration.sql:81-89` - `execute` on `is_salon_owner`/`is_salon_member` was not revoked from anon/public (harmless: returns false for anon).
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (`0001`, SEC-08). Execute revoked from anon/public, granted only to `authenticated`. RLS unaffected (every policy using them is `to authenticated`). Test green.

#### SEC-09 - Prompt-injection surface in outgoing AI messages · **Low** (architectural; live exploit not reproduced)
- **Evidence:** `src/lib/ai.functions.ts` - untrusted customer name and notes flowed directly into the AI prompt; the reminder output is then sent from the salon's own WhatsApp/SMS (`src/routes/_authenticated/customers.$id.tsx`).
- **Verification:** the production model is not reachable locally; two injection attempts against an equivalent model (used as a test tool) were not followed. The architectural weakness was real; a live exploit was not reproduced.
- **Fix / Status: Mitigated** (`src/lib/ai-sanitize.ts` + `ai.functions.ts`, SEC-09). Untrusted data is fenced as "data, not instructions" (and fence-escape attempts are stripped); URLs are stripped from the reminder output. Unit test: `audit/tests/ai-sanitize.test.ts`. **Why "Mitigated", not "Fixed":** the enforceable control is the URL stripping on the output; fencing the input lowers but cannot guarantee away prompt-injection, and no live exploit was run against the production model (not reachable here). This is defence-in-depth, not a proof.

#### SEC-10 - Personal-data flows (technical, not legal) · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** customer name/phone/email + notes + history are sent to the AI gateway and on to a language-model provider for the summary/reminder features (`src/lib/ai.functions.ts`); no retention limit, erasure or export; no privacy notice on the public booking page.
- **Fix / Status: Partially fixed.** A one-line privacy notice was added to the booking page (`src/routes/book.$slug.tsx`). **Recommended (not done):** minimize data sent to the model, retention/auto-deletion, export, and customer self-service erasure.

#### SEC-11 - `.env` committed; dependency advisories · **Low**
- **Evidence:** `.env` was tracked in the generated repo (only the publishable/anon key, which is public by design, so not critical, but committing env files is a bad habit). `npm audit`: 4 moderate advisories, all the dev-only esbuild dev-server issue via `drizzle-kit` (does not affect the production runtime).
- **Fix / Status: Partially addressed here** (`.env` untracked, `.env.example` added for this repo). **Recommended:** choose one package manager and pin the lockfile; update `drizzle-kit`.

#### SEC-12 - Authentication (GoTrue) behaviour · **Low** (mostly good; brute-force gap)
- **Evidence (test project):** password policy enforced server-side (a 3-char password is rejected, `422 weak_password`, "at least 6 characters"); email confirmation required (`mailer_autoconfirm = false`); no email enumeration via the password grant or signup (identical responses / obfuscated signup); anonymous sign-in disabled. **Gap:** 12 rapid wrong-password attempts were not throttled (no `429`).
- **Fix / Status: Left as recommendation** (verify production auth settings; add brute-force rate limiting / lockout). Values are from the test project and may differ in production.

### Correctness & maintainability (SE)

#### SE-01 - Business rules live in the UI, not the server · **Medium**
- Opening hours/days, the 21-day window, cancel/move, "staff own calendar", revenue - all in React. Same root cause as SEC-01/BH-01/SEC-03.
- **Fix / Status: Partially fixed.** The **public** booking rules were moved into the RPC (BH-01) and the role boundaries into RLS (SEC-03). Owner/staff cancel/move stays in the app by design (see [Design decisions](#design-decisions)). **Still in the browser:** revenue and popular-services aggregation, tracked separately as SE-03 (recommendation) - so this root-cause finding is not fully closed.

#### SE-02 - Time zone: slots computed in the visitor's browser zone · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** `src/lib/format.ts` used `date.setHours(...)` (browser-local); `open_time`/`close_time` are stored as bare wall-clock with no zone. Test (`audit/tests/timezone.test.ts`): the same "09:00" resolved to 06:00Z (Istanbul), 07:00Z (Berlin = 10:00 local), 13:00Z (New York = 16:00 local).
- **Impact:** a visitor outside the salon's zone saw shifted times and could book a slot that is not 09:00 at the salon; two visitors in different zones picking "09:00" sent two different instants.
- **Fix / Status: Fixed** (with BH-01). `buildSlots` now takes a `timeZone` and computes slots in the salon's zone (`zonedWallTimeToUtc`); callers pass `salon.timezone`; `get_public_salon` returns it. Test green under three time zones.

#### SE-03 - Scale: no pagination; default row cap; client-side revenue · **Medium**
- **Evidence:** list queries in `src/hooks/use-bookings.ts` have no range/limit; the dashboard computes revenue client-side. Verified over HTTP: with 1100 bookings, the REST API returned only 1000 (`content-range: 0-999/1100`), so lists and the dashboard silently under-report past 1000 rows.
- **Fix / Status: Left as recommendation.** Move revenue/stats to the server (RPC/SQL); add pagination and explicit ranges.

#### SE-04 - Data model · **Medium**
- Customer identity keyed by `(salon_id, phone)` with no normalization; cascade deletes; services keep a price/name snapshot on bookings (good); deactivating staff leaves their future bookings; no `updated_at`/audit trail.
- **Fix / Status: Partially fixed.** Phone numbers are now normalized before storage (`normalize_phone()`), with uniqueness on the normalized value (test green: different formats map to one customer). **Recommended:** soft-delete and `updated_at`/audit trail.

#### SE-05 - Quality & maintainability · **Low**
- One test in the generated app (routing); some `any` in `src/lib/ai.functions.ts`; `customer_notes` has no UPDATE policy (notes are not editable by anyone - minor); vendor lock-in (managed backend, AI gateway, vendor packages).
- **Fix / Status: Left as recommendation.** (This repo adds a runnable security test suite under `audit/tests/`.)

---

## 5. What was done well (with evidence)

Confirmed by the passing ("green") tests or by code review:

| Area | Evidence |
|---|---|
| RLS enabled on all six tables; tenants genuinely isolated | `role-matrix.test.ts` - B/X/anon cannot read or write Salon A (green) |
| Visitors never touch tables; public actions go only through 3 security-definer RPCs | matrix (anon `select` denied) + `0000_migration.sql:174-176` |
| Double-booking prevented by a gist exclusion constraint | `0000_migration.sql:58`; `public-booking.test.ts` (green) |
| Past-dated and cross-salon bookings rejected | `public-booking.test.ts` (green) |
| Anon cannot forge a price (price comes from the service) | `pentest.test.ts` (green) |
| `create_salon` cannot forge the owner (always `auth.uid()`) | `pentest.test.ts` (green) |
| Service duration must be positive (CHECK constraint) | `pentest.test.ts` (green) |
| AI calls require authentication and run with the user's token, so AI cannot reach another salon's customer | `ai.functions.ts`; `auth-middleware.ts` |
| The service-role key stays server-side, not in the client bundle | `client.server.ts` |
| CSRF middleware re-enabled for server functions | `src/start.ts` |
| React auto-escaping: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user data, so stored XSS in names/notes is neutralized | code review |
| Error page / boundary do not leak stack traces; cron auth uses constant-time comparison | `error-page.ts`, `cron-auth.ts` |
| No source maps in the production public assets | build output |

Lovable's own scan reported no issues and states that *"The scanner can't catch every possible risk"* - which is consistent with these findings, since they are about rules the UI enforces but the API does not.

---

## 6. Remaining recommendations (not changed in this round)

- **SEC-01:** phone verification (OTP) at booking time (overwrite is already blocked; residual linkage remains).
- **BH-02:** per-IP rate limiting + CAPTCHA (edge layer) and a per-user/salon AI quota.
- **SEC-06:** HttpOnly cookie session instead of localStorage.
- **SEC-10 / data model:** minimize data sent to the model, retention/auto-deletion, export, customer self-service erasure; soft-delete and `updated_at`/audit trail.
- **SEC-11:** keep `.env` out of git; single package manager + pinned lockfile + `drizzle-kit` update.
- **SE-03:** pagination + server-side aggregation (the ~1000-row cap is real).
- **SE-05:** broaden test coverage; replace `any` with typed query results.
- **SEC-05:** a stricter nonce-based CSP (the current policy allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`).

Suggested next priority: SEC-01 OTP -> SEC-06 cookie session -> SE-03 pagination/server aggregation -> retention/erasure (SEC-10).
